sections.content: Bend, Oregon sits at an interesting crossroads right now. It's no longer a hidden gem — everyone from California transplants to institutional investors knows about it. But that doesn't mean the opportunity is gone. Savvy investors who know where to look are still finding real estate deals in Bend OR that pencil out nicely. You just need the right strategy, the right data, and a willingness to dig deeper than the MLS. Whether you're brand new to real estate or a seasoned wholesaler expanding your market, this guide breaks down exactly what's happening in Bend and how to position yourself for profit. If you're just getting started, bookmark our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide first — it'll give you the foundation you need to make sense of everything we cover here.
Bend OR Real Estate Market Overview: What the Numbers Say

Bend is the largest city in Deschutes County and has been one of the fastest-growing cities in the entire United States for over a decade. The population has grown from roughly 52,000 in 2010 to more than 102,000 today, and that growth shows no signs of stopping. The city benefits from a rare combination of outdoor recreation, a thriving tech and remote-work culture, strong tourism, and limited buildable land constrained by the urban growth boundary. All of these factors create persistent demand pressure on housing.

As of mid-2025, the median home price in Bend sits around $685,000 — down slightly from the pandemic peak of roughly $750,000 in 2022, but still up significantly from $425,000 in 2019. Days on market have stretched from the frenzied 7-10 days of 2021 to a more measured 30-45 days today. That cooling is actually good news for investors. It means motivated sellers have more time to sit with their frustration, and deals that would have been snapped up by owner-occupants in a weekend are now staying available long enough for investors to conduct proper due diligence.

Markets that cool off don't stop producing deals — they just reward preparation over panic. In Bend, the investors winning right now are the ones who built their systems before the opportunity showed up.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Deals in Bend OR
Not all of Bend is created equal from an investor's standpoint. Prices, rental demand, and deal availability vary significantly by submarket. Here's a breakdown of the areas worth focusing on.
Old Bend and the Westside

The Westside, including the historic Old Bend neighborhood, is where the city's character lives. Craftsman bungalows, walkable streets, and proximity to the Deschutes River make this area perennially desirable. Median prices here run $750,000–$950,000, which makes wholesale deals harder to find but fix-and-flip opportunities excellent for experienced investors. ARVs in this area hold strong because buyer demand never fully dries up.
Southeast Bend

Southeast Bend is the working-class backbone of the city and the single best area for value-add rental deals. Homes here run $450,000–$600,000, and you'll find a higher concentration of long-term homeowners, aging properties with deferred maintenance, and sellers who may be open to creative terms. If you're building a buy-and-hold portfolio, this is where your time-on-door knocking pays off. Gross rental yields in Southeast Bend can hit 5–6.5% on well-positioned properties, which is strong for this market.
Redmond (the Bend Adjacent Play)

Redmond, just 17 miles north of Bend, deserves its own mention. With median prices hovering around $425,000–$475,000 and strong rental demand from Bend workers priced out of the city itself, Redmond offers some of the best cash flow math in the entire Central Oregon market. Many investors targeting real estate deals in Bend OR actually end up closing their best deals in Redmond. Explore our dedicated [Bend OR market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/bend-or) for current deal flow data across both cities.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Bend Right Now
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling in Bend is possible but requires more work than a lower-priced market. Because median values are high, your end buyers (flippers and landlords) need strong margins, which means you need to find properties with significant distress or seller motivation. Estate sales, pre-foreclosures, tired landlords with aging Section 8 properties, and divorce situations are your best sources. Assignment fees of $15,000–$35,000 are realistic on well-structured deals. New to the wholesale model? Our guide on [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) walks through the entire process step by step.
Fix and Flip

Bend's strong ARVs make it an attractive flip market for experienced investors. A typical flip scenario in Southeast Bend might look like this: purchase a 3-bed/2-bath at $480,000, invest $85,000 in renovations, and sell for $650,000 — producing a gross profit of roughly $85,000 before holding costs and financing. That's a meaningful return, but it requires accurate ARV analysis upfront. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) before you make any offer to make sure your numbers hold up under scrutiny.
Long-Term and Short-Term Rentals

Bend's tourism economy — Mount Bachelor skiing, the Deschutes River, mountain biking, and hiking — makes short-term rentals (STRs) genuinely viable here in ways they aren't in most markets. A well-positioned STR near downtown or the Old Mill District can gross $60,000–$90,000 annually. However, the City of Bend has implemented STR licensing requirements and caps, so due diligence on local ordinances is essential before buying for this strategy. Long-term rentals in Southeast Bend and Redmond offer steadier, more predictable cash flow for investors who prefer lower management intensity.

Pro Tip: Before running any deal in Bend, plug your numbers into the free [Wholesale Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) at AIWholesail. It accounts for ARV, repair costs, holding costs, and your target profit margin — and it takes less than two minutes to use. In a high-price market like Bend, getting the math wrong by even 5% can turn a profit into a loss.
Local Market Trends Every Bend Investor Should Know

items: Inventory is rising slowly: Active listings in Deschutes County have increased roughly 18% year-over-year as of mid-2025, giving buyers more negotiating power than any point since 2019.
Remote work demand is stabilizing: The pandemic-era surge of California and Washington transplants has slowed, but Bend's desirability as a remote work destination remains well above pre-2020 levels.
New construction is limited: The urban growth boundary restricts sprawl, keeping resale values supported even as buyer competition softens.

Interest rate sensitivity is high: Bend's high price point means monthly payment swings on rate changes are larger than most markets. Deals with seller financing or assumable mortgages carry extra value here.
Rental vacancy rates remain tight: Deschutes County's rental vacancy sits below 4%, meaning well-priced rentals lease quickly and income streams are reliable for buy-and-hold investors.

sections.content: How to Find Off-Market Deals in Bend OR

The best real estate deals in Bend OR almost never hit the MLS. By the time a distressed property is listed publicly, it's been cleaned up enough to attract retail buyers and its investor upside has narrowed. The real opportunity lives in off-market channels. Direct mail to absentee owners, driving for dollars in Southeast Bend and Redmond, building relationships with probate attorneys and estate sale companies, and networking with local property managers (who often know about landlords ready to sell) are all proven methods. For a comprehensive breakdown of these strategies, read our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals).
Tips for Out-of-State Investors Eyeing Bend OR
Bend attracts a lot of out-of-state investor interest, which is both a validation of the market and a warning sign. Here's how to compete effectively without being on the ground.

items: Build a local team first: Find a real estate-friendly agent who works with investors, a local contractor with a proven track record on flips, and a property manager before you close your first deal. Bend has a tight contractor market — availability and pricing are very different from lower-cost metros.

Visit before you buy: Bend's neighborhoods vary dramatically within short distances. A $500,000 house on one street can be a great rental; the same price two blocks away may sit in a flood zone or have access issues. One site visit saves you from months of headaches.

Understand Oregon landlord-tenant law: Oregon is a tenant-friendly state with specific notice requirements, rent control provisions in some contexts, and mandatory relocation assistance in certain eviction scenarios. Know the rules before you own a rental here.

Run conservative numbers: Out-of-state investors often underestimate repair costs in Bend. Labor is expensive, materials ship far, and older homes often have surprises. Add a 15–20% contingency to any rehab budget. Use our guide on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) to build a bulletproof analysis process.

Leverage data tools: Platforms that aggregate off-market leads, distressed property signals, and deal comparables are worth every penny when you're investing remotely. The time you save on research directly impacts your ability to move fast when a deal appears.

sections.content: The biggest mistake out-of-state investors make in Bend is treating it like a Phoenix or Indianapolis. This market rewards relationships and local knowledge above almost everything else. Build your network before you need it.
Is Bend OR the Right Market for You?

Bend isn't the right market for every investor. If you need deals under $300,000 to make your cash-flow numbers work, you'll struggle here. If you're an experienced flipper comfortable with higher price points and strong ARVs, or a short-term rental operator who understands tourism markets, Bend can be excellent. The key is going in with clear eyes, accurate data, and a strategy that fits the local conditions rather than trying to force a strategy that works in a different market onto Bend's unique dynamics.
